Best Board Games for Beginners: 5 Games to Start Your Collection

2026-09-06

I bought my first modern board game in 2022. It was a mistake. I picked something called "Terraforming Mars" because Reddit said it was the best game ever. Three hours later, my friends were asleep and I had read 14 pages of rules. The game sat on my shelf for six months.

So here is what I wish someone told me. Start with games that take 30 minutes to learn and 45 minutes to play. Not 90 minute brain burners with 12 page rulebooks.

I have about 35 games on my shelf now. Some were hits. Some were misses. These 5 are the ones I actually bring to game night. The rest just collect dust.

1. Catan. The Gateway That Keeps On Giving.

Catan is the game that started the modern board game boom. You roll dice, collect resources, trade with neighbors, build settlements. It takes 75 minutes but the turns are fast.

What surprised me: it is not about strategy. It is about negotiation. "I will give you two sheep if you give me one brick." That bargaining keeps even quiet players talking. I have seen groups of strangers become friends over a game of Catan. The 6th Edition is around $49.99 on Amazon and comes with updated components. One thing to know: it only plays 3-4 players, so pick up the 5-6 player expansion if your group is bigger. Worth every penny.

2. Ticket to Ride. Simple Routes, Big Fun.

Ticket to Ride is about building train routes across America. Draw cards. Claim routes. Connect cities. That is the whole game.

But the tension is real. You watch your friend grab the route you needed. You sweat over going for the long cross-country connection or playing it safe. The first time I played, I got blocked by my girlfriend and she laughed at me. I still lost. It plays 45 minutes, supports 2-5 players, and costs $49.99. This is the game I buy as a gift for people who say they don't like board games.

3. Azul. Pretty and Mean.

Azul might be the most beautiful game I own. You draft colorful ceramic tiles and place them on your board. They clack when you pick them up. It feels expensive.

Do not let the pretty look fool you though. Azul is savage. If you take tiles you cannot place, they go on the floor line and lose you points. Someone will definitely stick you with a pile of tiles you do not want. My wife got so mad at one game she refused to play again for a month. Then she asked to play again the next week. It plays in 40 minutes, 2-4 players, and costs $31.99. Get the version with the improved scoring board.

4. Splendor. The Engine Builder That Clicks.

Splendor is where you learn what "engine building" means. You collect gem tokens. You buy development cards. You attract nobles to your court. Early rounds feel slow. By round 10, your engine is humming and you are pulling cards every turn.

The first time I played, I did not understand the hype. It felt simple. Too simple. Then I saw my friend chain three moves into a win and I got it. It is the perfect second game for new players. Deeper than Catan but still plays in 30 minutes. $38.99 on Amazon and supports 2-4 players.

5. Love Letter. 16 Cards. Zero Fat.

Love Letter has 16 cards. That is it. Sixteen cards and a bag of tokens. It costs $12.99. It plays in 20 minutes. And it has more tension than most games with a hundred cards.

You are trying to deliver a love letter to the princess while eliminating rival suitors. Each card has a power. The deduction game is real. You can lose in the first 30 seconds if you draw the wrong card. I take this game to every gathering. I keep it in my work bag. Someone always wants to play again. It is the best $12 you will ever spend on a game.

The Bottom Line

I learned the hard way that "best game ever on Reddit" and "best game for your group" are very different things. Start with Catan or Ticket to Ride. Then try Azul or Splendor. By then you will know what you like. That is how collections grow. Not by buying the top 10 list from BGG.
